rounds.text: IKIO trades at an expensive P/E of 38 and a price-to-book of 2.62x, while a discounted cash flow model puts intrinsic value at Rs 100 per share against a market price of Rs 204, leaving a severe margin of safety of -104.9% [E1, E2, E34, E35]. The reverse DCF indicates that today's price already implies 16.8% earnings growth, which far outpaces the 7.0% assumed in the base case [E36]. Profitability metrics remain depressed, with a low ROE of 7.1% and a 3-year median ROE of just 9%, compounded by a 3-year profit contraction of -6% and a severe long-term operating margin contraction of 9 percentage points down to 13% [E7, E12, E17, E19]. Cash generation fails to support the reported earnings, illustrated by a weak cash conversion of 0.38x, operating cash flow at only 37% of operating profit, and a steep negative free cash flow of Rs -65 Cr alongside mounting borrowings [E23, E25, E26, E28]. Furthermore, institutional confidence has eroded dramatically as foreign and domestic institutional holdings plummeted by 2.49 and 6.62 percentage points respectively since September 2023, driving negative money flow [E31, E32, E33]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has been solid at 23% over 5 years and 18% over 3 years, and the company operates within a consumer durables sector tailwind [E8, E9, E64].
